data.note:
My call of Microtubule stabilizers was incorrect; unblinded compound is MG-132 (PubChem CID 462382) annotated as Protein degradation.

Reflection: the tubulin-bright rounded phenotype at 3-10 uM (tub_mean z up to +116, act_tub_ratio strongly down) and 15/20 stabilizer atlas neighbours (docetaxel, taxol, epothilone B) drove the call, confirmed by microscopist. In retrospect proteasome inhibition produces a convergent mitotic-arrest phenotype with stabilized microtubule-kinetochore attachments and condensed tubulin masses, explaining the mimicry. The clue I underweighted was the high-similarity Protein degradation neighbour ALLN (sim 0.827) and the 30 uM collapse with toxicity, consistent with proteasome-inhibitor-induced apoptosis and stress described for MG-132 (e.g. PMID 21499287, PMID 21203833, PMID 18435911) and mitotic microtubule-kinetochore stability regulation (PMID 17525528).

Follow-up in a real lab: ubiquitin-conjugate accumulation assay plus phospho-H3 / cyclin B to test proteasome blockade vs direct tubulin binding.

reflection.text:
The tubulin signal was real and replicated: 10 uM rep1 tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0 and tub_mean z=+116.4 (e2) reproduced in 3 uM (e8) and 10 uM rep2 tub_glcm_contrast z=+89.6 (e9), with microscopist rounding/density loss (e5) and 15/20 atlas neighbors calling Microtubule stabilizers (e6, e11). That consistency plus very large effect sizes drove confidence to 0.91 for stabilizers.

What misled was treating a secondary phenotype as primary. Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 causes accumulation of cell-cycle regulators and mitotic arrest, which can appear as bright, textured tubulin and rounding. I over-weighted a 14-cell well (e2) where low n inflates z-scores, dismissed that the atlas did contain Protein degradation 1/10 in both runs (e6, e11), and rationalized away the contradictory dose_response rho=-0.03 p=0.96 (e12) and the 30 uM collapse in nuc_solidity z=-414.8 and act_tub_ratio z=-159.3 (e4) as toxicity hook rather than non-monotonicity inconsistent with a simple stabilizer.

The acquisition choice compounded this: I sampled to confirm monotonic tubulin rise from 0.3 to 10 uM but did not acquire proteasome-specific readouts or a direct tubulin control comparison, and stopped after visual and atlas agreement. The flat dose-response should have triggered down-weighting and explicit testing of Protein degradation versus mitotic alternatives.

Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 modulates cell survival pathways, consistent with broad secondary phenotypes beyond tubulin.
Perturbation of mitotic checkpoint signaling can alter microtubule-kinetochore attachment stability, providing a mechanism for secondary stabilizer-like tubulin phenotypes.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean profile across three independent measurements with very large effect sizes; alternative mitotic or actin mechanisms cannot reproduce the combined tubulin hyper-intensity and cytological rounding, and the reference-atlas mapping is structurally discriminatory. Best-fit class is microtubule stabilization rather than destabilization. Minor incompleteness remains: the upper-dose toxicity hook is sparsely sampled, but it is not needed to separate stabilization from depolymerization.

## Unblinding

Compound: **MG-132** (PubChem CID [462382](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/462382))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

The tubulin signal was real and replicated: 10 uM rep1 tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0 and tub_mean z=+116.4 (e2) reproduced in 3 uM (e8) and 10 uM rep2 tub_glcm_contrast z=+89.6 (e9), with microscopist rounding/density loss (e5) and 15/20 atlas neighbors calling Microtubule stabilizers (e6, e11). That consistency plus very large effect sizes drove confidence to 0.91 for stabilizers.

What misled was treating a secondary phenotype as primary. Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 causes accumulation of cell-cycle regulators and mitotic arrest, which can appear as bright, textured tubulin and rounding. I over-weighted a 14-cell well (e2) where low n inflates z-scores, dismissed that the atlas did contain Protein degradation 1/10 in both runs (e6, e11), and rationalized away the contradictory dose_response rho=-0.03 p=0.96 (e12) and the 30 uM collapse in nuc_solidity z=-414.8 and act_tub_ratio z=-159.3 (e4) as toxicity hook rather than non-monotonicity inconsistent with a simple stabilizer.

The acquisition choice compounded this: I sampled to confirm monotonic tubulin rise from 0.3 to 10 uM but did not acquire proteasome-specific readouts or a direct tubulin control comparison, and stopped after visual and atlas agreement. The flat dose-response should have triggered down-weighting and explicit testing of Protein degradation versus mitotic alternatives.

What was right:
- Tubulin hyper-intensity and texture increase were replicated across 3 uM and two 10 uM wells (e2, e8, e9), not a single-well artifact
- Cell rounding / solidity loss and lower density noted by microscopy (e5) correctly flagged mitotic / cytotoxic effect with large effect sizes
- Reference atlas did flag Protein degradation as a minority neighbor in both runs (e6, e11), preserving the true class in the data

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted secondary stabilizer-like tubulin bundling from MG-132 proteasome inhibition as primary microtubule stabilization
- Ignored flat tub_mean dose-response rho=-0.03 (e12) that contradicted expected monotonic stabilizer increase
- Over-weighted e2 with only 14 cells and extreme z-scores (+328, +116) without accounting for low-n variance
- Dismissed 30 uM phenotype collapse (e4) and minority Protein degradation atlas hits instead of testing them as competing hypothesis

Proposed next experiment: Compare MG-132 dose-response to paclitaxel and bortezomib controls with parallel readouts: proteasome activity by fluorogenic Suc-LLVY-AMC cleavage and K48-ubiquitin accumulation plus in vitro tubulin polymerization and phospho-H3 mitotic index to test direct tubulin stabilization versus secondary mitotic arrest from proteasome inhibition.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [21499287](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21499287/): Proteasome inhibitor MG-132 induces C6 glioma cell apoptosis via oxidative stress. *Acta Pharmacol Sin* (2011) — MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor that induces apoptosis, supporting Protein degradation as the true MoA rather than direct microtubule stabilization.
- PMID [30695709](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30695709/): Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 protects against deltamethrin-induced apoptosis in rat hippocampus. *Life Sci* (2019) — Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 modulates cell survival pathways, consistent with broad secondary phenotypes beyond tubulin.
- PMID [17525528](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17525528/): BubR1 and CENP-E have antagonistic effects upon the stability of microtubule-kinetochore attachments in Drosophila S2 cell mitosis. *Cell Cycle* (2007) — Perturbation of mitotic checkpoint signaling can alter microtubule-kinetochore attachment stability, providing a mechanism for secondary stabilizer-like tubulin phenotypes.
